- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to revert; apply a mild downward bias to prevent over-optimism.  
- If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by 1–2% over 3–5 days, model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast slightly in next horizon if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.30) mid-horizon, model often lags in adjusting upward; apply a small upward bias to catch momentum.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by 2–3% over 10+ days, model underestimates mean reversion; consider adding a small upward drift component in next forecast.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves when sentiment is mixed or mildly positive — model tends to overreact to negative sentiment; use smoothing or lagged sentiment to dampen extreme predictions.
